standard_prerequisites: Impurities above a point, and the base change of the relative assassin of a module
The existence of an etale chart of a fibre product through a prescribed pair of points, and the resulting flatness of the induced morphism of schemes
Lifting of specialisations along a flat morphism of schemes, and the compatibility of the closed subspace cut out by a point with the base change
core_obligations: Choose a scheme etale over the fibre product of the new base with the old test scheme, together with a point lying over both the given point of the new base and the given point of the test scheme
Record that the induced morphism to the old test scheme is flat at that point, so that the specialisation in the old test scheme lifts to one in the new test scheme
Choose a point of the base changed total space lying over the lifted specialisation and lying in the relative assassin, using base change of the relative assassin, and compare closures

Conclude that the image of the closure of that point cannot contain the chosen point of the new test scheme, because its image under the comparison map lies in the closure of the original point, which does not contain the projected point
proof_roadmap: Build etale charts of the fibre product through the prescribed pair of points
Lift the specialisation along the flat induced morphism
Pick an associated point over the lifted specialisation and compare closures to obtain an impurity
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the ascent of impurities along a flat base change at source lines 365-375, label lemma-flat-ascent-impurity, whose proof occupies source lines 377-399. The proof is a construction: it chooses an etale chart of the fibre product of the new base with the old test scheme through the prescribed pair of points, observes that the induced morphism to the old test scheme is flat at that point so that the given specialisation lifts, and then uses base change of the relative assassin to find a point of the base changed total space lying over the lifted specialisation and still in the relative assassin. The impurity then follows from comparing closures: the closure of the chosen point maps into the closure of the original point, which misses the projected point, so the image of the closure cannot contain the new base point. The counted statement records neither the chart choice nor the closure comparison.
